01.project.v: Willis Temby: Custom Website Design and Build (plus logo redesign)

01.pm.v: Gabe Silva (project coordinator from 21/10/2026, took over from Eleanor Morgan; earlier Tafleen and Mia). Adam Barbarich stays involved at kick-off, design sign-off, pre-launch and post-launch

01.dev_reviewer.v: Raf Baldasso (head of development, across the technical scope since sales)

01.design_hours.v: 34 design hours in the quote, not split between homepage and internals. Revisions and adjustments (dev and design) are a separate 21 hours

01.deliverable.v: Homepage, Contact page, industry landing template, policy/product template, Our People team profile, blog and news/insights template, plus internal page designs as required. Logo: 3 concepts, 2 revision rounds, basic style guide

01.platform.v: WordPress (latest stable), Gravity Forms, Rank Math Premium

01.kickoff_held.v: Yes, 21/07/2026 online. Mia Mammoliti with Isabella and Cameron (Willis Temby). Raf absent

02.drive.v: Willis Temby folder (Drive id 1yaFpFcI1J7SM0lBZ0WMWCfoSVG-Jl8TM): Brand Brief, Home Page Layout, Website 2.0 Flow v2, Product Page mock-up

02.sitemap.v: Sitemap V2 (Whimsical, https://whimsical.com/EJkF24AZeYxzYnSYJugz7V): Isabella's changes from 29/10 applied on 30/10. Sent for approval. Mia's earlier board (willis-temby-RgkYfRiPhmGzJuYmw73Msa) is superseded.

02.existing_site.v: willistemby.com.au on RocketSpark. A full break, not a reference: new logo and colours, almost every page rewritten, "pretty much a different website". The main reason for the rebuild is that the current site is not responsive and forms are slow.

02.style_guide.v: No brand style guide exists yet. The logo line item delivers a basic style guide for logo use and colour palettes

02.logo.v: Final logo chosen: option on page 1 of the Figma logo file (https://www.figma.com/proto/8Dr9ef5tOOeBQ0T6psGGOP/Willis-Temby-Logo, node 267-793), "WillisTemby" written as one word with no space. It closely resembles Miramar's mark, so the website design must set Willis Temby apart from Miramar.

02.moodboard.v: Client moodboard (bold colour pops, kept professional) and AI-generated style ideas in the old MASTER Logo Brief; Brand Brief.docx

02.quote.v: Estimate 5756, Digital Partnership: Custom Website Design and Build for Willis Temby, signed by Isabella Popov 30/06/2026

02.handover.v: Willis Temby Internal Handover Brief, Scott Donovan

03.who.v: Australian-owned, privately operated insurance brokerage, founded 1984, 7 Alvan Street Mount Lawley. Legal entity Willis Temby Insurance Brokers Pty Ltd, AFSL 233 765, ABN 85 009 087 585. Rebranding to "Willis Temby"

03.what.v: Risk advisory and management, claims advocacy and tailored insurance for corporate and commercial clients. Also program review, early injury intervention through Praventus for workers' compensation clients, and premium funding.

03.for_whom.v: Mid to large commercial businesses in high-risk sectors (marine, mining and resources, construction, agribusiness, commercial property). Buyers: owners, CFOs, CEOs, MDs, risk managers

03.why_us.v: "Strategic insurance and risk advice that helps businesses grow with confidence." Client-focused, educates clients, a team that refines policies to get clients the best result. 40+ years.

03.position.v: Repositioning from a WA broker to an Australian one: "we don't really want to be saying that we are from WA". One director sits on the National Insurance Brokers Association board. Wants visitors to see "professional, smart, and we can get the job done", with an easy process that still looks intelligent, "without making it look stupid". Must sit clearly apart from Willis Towers Watson.

03.decision_makers.v: Isabella Breheny (Head of Marketing and Communications, the only marketing person) runs it day to day. Sign-off is "all of us, together": Isabella, Alex Rowland and Brett Piggott. Formal approvals go to the weekly team meeting, so allow about a week per round; small questions about 2 days. Only Isabella has attended a kick-off; the directors have not been on a call.

03.behaviour.v: Fast, considered, decisive. Runs things past the directors and comes back with clear positions. Prefers fortnightly milestone updates over weekly check-ins. Pushes back on scope, not price

04.objective.v: Be found online and convert more form submissions, so new business does not rely only on referrals and the directors being out and about. Reposition as a trusted Australian brokerage nationwide. Australia only for the next 2 to 3 years.

04.hero_action.v: Contact us, as the highlighted menu button.

04.secondary_actions.v: Lodge a Claim and Pay an Invoice, both under Contact in the menu. Request a Quote and Workplace Injury are menu links.

04.success.v: Match or beat Phoenix Insurance organic traffic (661 a month) within 12 months; long term overtake Centrewest (1,000+ a month); lift form enquiries from about 1 a month

04.broken.v: About 1 form a month against 600+ calls, slow contact form, jQuery 1.7.2 security exposure, placeholder content, no alt tags, multiple H1s, "Powered by RocketSpark" footer, no AI search presence, dated brand

04.keep.v: Legal entity name and AFSL details on site. Existing URLs and rankings via the SEO migration. Brand moves to the new logo and its colours.

05.profile.v: B2B, SME to enterprise, strong mid-market bias. Personal lines exist for existing clients but are not the focus

05.primary_audience.v: Owners, CEOs, CFOs, managing directors, operations directors and risk managers of mid to large commercial businesses in high-risk and specialised sectors: marine, mining and resources, construction, energy, medical and property.

05.secondary_audience.v: Aviation, transport, healthcare, manufacturing, professional services, cyber, hospitality. HNW individuals for personal assets

05.worries.v: Not asked in the room. From the brief: whether the broker is credible enough for a complex program and understands their industry, not price.
05.worries.who: Muiz to design for credibility; confirm at homepage presentation

05.devices.v: Not known. Pull from GA4 once access is granted.

05.competitors.v: Centrewest, Knightcorp, Lockton, Howden, EBM (client's list). Bellrock Advisory is a liked site, not a competitor.

06.value.v: $35,840 ex GST ($39,424 inc GST) fixed estimate at $195 an hour, including the $2,495 logo option. Hosting $45 a month ex GST for 12 months

06.design_allocation.v: 34 design hours inside 155 website hours (Dev 66, PM 26, QA 8, Revisions 21). Logo is its own $2,495 line. Split between homepage and internals not set

06.revisions.v: Design: 2 major rounds per layout. Development: 2 rounds of changes. Logo: 2 rounds on the chosen concept

06.in_scope.v: Logo redesign; WordPress build; mega menu with clickable parents; Gravity Forms (general enquiry, request a quote, lodge a claim, workplace injury, insurance program review); secure PDF storage for claim and injury forms; Pay an Invoice page linking to DEFT (Macquarie); FAQ accordions; blog and insights with filtering; team profiles; EDM integration; LinkedIn feed; testimonials; schema; compliance content and AFSL footer; content migration (placement only, 14 hours); SEO migration (9 hours); training; 30-day support

06.out_scope.v: Accessibility audit and WCAG remediation; content writing, restructuring or rewriting; a true payment gateway (Stripe, Ebix) or WinBEAT NEXT API; client portal; photography and video; SEO retainer; Google Ads; annual third-party subscriptions

06.future.v: Video for the homepage banner and team headshots: client asked for a quote (29/10), PWD to quote separately. Parked: client portal via WinBEAT NEXT API (12 to 18 months), SEO retainer, Google Ads, ongoing content.

06.sensitivities.v: Signature comment: "discussions on new site map will overrule that listed within contract". Quote describes 12 verticals and 13 product lines; the client's new sitemap is about 109 to 125 pages. Directors' top concern is scope creep: anything new is quoted in writing first. Rate locked at $195 for the project

08.photography.v: PWD uses generic placeholder and stock images; the client is not expected to supply them. The client supplies its own photos: team headshots and more team photos are planned for the new year, so the 17 profiles need a placeholder state until then. Photography is out of the quote; PWD can quote it separately.

08.icons.v: Wants a standalone element pulled from the logo (like Centrewest's C) and a custom icon set reusable across marketing

08.video.v: Opening video banner like tattarang.com: one continuous shot, boat to road to mine site, covering more of their industries, with the headline over it. Client asked for a video quote; PWD to quote separately (possibly with headshots). Design uses a still or placeholder until footage exists.

09.sitemap_status.v: DRAFT, sent for approval. V2 carries every change from Isabella's email of 29/10.

09.total_pages.v: 104 pages to build (Sitemap V2): homepage, sector landing and 36 sector pages, risk landing and 30 risk pages, 4 About pages, Our People listing and 17 profiles, Insights, Contact and 4 linked pages, 2 Advisory Team pages, 5 policy pages. Commission Consent Declaration form not counted yet. Insights articles move across and are not counted.
09.total_pages.contested: Quote describes 12 verticals and 13 product lines, 25 pages [E]; Sitemap V2 has 66 sector and risk pages. Client signed: new sitemap overrules the contract [E]. Designs are covered by items 3 and 4; build and migration hours for the extra pages are the risk. Agree a position with Adam.

09.top_nav.v: Sector, Risk, About, Insights, Contact as a mega menu. Contact is the highlighted button, with Pay an Invoice, Lodge a Claim, Request a Quote and Workplace Injury underneath. Middle groupings (e.g. Agriculture) are labels, not pages.

09.utility_nav.v: Under Contact: Pay an Invoice, Lodge a Claim, Request a Quote, Workplace Injury.

09.footer.v: AFSL 233 765 disclosure and legal entity name are non-negotiable, plus compliance links

11.designs_quoted.v: 5 internal templates named in the quote (Contact, industry landing, policy/product, Our People, blog/news), plus "internal page designs as required", which covers About, Our Process, Community & ESG and Careers

11.hours.v: Not split in the quote. Internals share the 34 design hours with the homepage

11.deliverable.v: Desktop and mobile per template ("designed for both mobile and desktop")

11.start.v: Homepage now, presented Friday 06/11/2026. Internal designs after Sitemap V2 is approved and the homepage direction is agreed.

11.order.v: Policy/product template first (it carries 66 sector and risk pages), then sector landing, Our People, Contact and forms, Insights, About pages, policy pages.

12.features.v: See 06.in_scope. Plus hover effects and micro-interactions, video and image support, spam protection

12.plugins.v: Gravity Forms and Rank Math Premium under PWD agency licences (no cost while hosted with PWD)

12.integrations.v: DEFT card portal scrapped: card payers use Arteva Pay, bank transfer via Macquarie continues; Pay an Invoice links to these. Forms move from Jotform to Gravity Forms as quoted. EDM: in scope, no tool chosen; client asks for it to be connected but not live until they are ready.
12.integrations.who: Raf: confirm EDM can be connected without going live

12.forms.v: Six forms. General enquiry, Request a quote, Insurance program review (optional upload): to camerong@, alexr@ and communications@. Lodge a claim (uploads): to the staff member picked in a dropdown, plus teambrett@ and teamalex@ if "not sure". Workplace injury (uploads): picked staff member, injury.management@, eoss@rtozerconsulting.com.au and nick@praventus.com.au. Commission Consent Declaration (signature): picked staff member and communications@. Uploads: PDF, JPG/PNG, Word, large files such as video. Marketing consent on the contact form. Client asked whether claim and injury could merge into one branching form; keep separate if simpler.
12.forms.who: Gabe with Raf: signature, branching and the 6th form against the quote
12.forms.contested: Quote names 5 forms; Commission Consent Declaration with a signature is a 6th. Branching merge not quoted.

12.accessibility.v: No WCAG target. Client has little accessibility experience and is "happy to be guided"; audit and remediation are out of scope, so build to sensible defaults.

12.performance.v: Fast loading is a must, forms especially: the current forms take seconds to load and lose people. The hero video must not slow the page.

12.seo.v: Keep rankings with 301s: the client's DRAFT website data lists where old URLs redirect. Retain GA4 and GTM, schema. Client says Adam mentioned the team would suggest optimised meta descriptions; not a quote line. Access to GA4, GTM, Search Console, domain and RocketSpark not returned in QB5. Domain managed by their IT.
12.seo.who: Gabe: QB5 access by phone; Adam: meta descriptions

12.browsers.v: Mobile and tablet friendly across all breakpoints

13.writer.v: Client writes all copy (Isabella's team). PWD places and splits it into sections

13.status.v: About 90 pages rewritten for the new sitemap. DRAFT website content and DRAFT website data (metadata, policies, experts, one-liners, redirect URLs) are in the Content folder, waiting on executive approval. Home Page Layout gives final homepage text. Product page PDF mentioned in the 29/10 email is not in the folder yet.

13.tone.v: Professional, assured not aggressive, expert but relatable, clear and concise, not overly corporate

13.in_time.v: Not for internals. Client expects the team to review copy in November and December, when work slows down. Design proceeds on the draft text.

13.internal_content.v: Draft copy for internal pages is in the Content folder. Workers' Compensation needs extra segments beyond the standard risk page.
13.internal_content.who: Muiz: confirm Workers' Compensation fits the policy/product template

14.intricacies.v: Sitemap rewritten twice (Mia, then the client's edits on 29/10); middle menu tiers must not become pages; DEFT scrapped for Arteva Pay; two names for the main contact (Popov and Breheny); logo resembles Miramar; Commission Consent Declaration is a 6th form with a signature.

14.risks.v: Copy: 90 pages waiting on executive approval for 2 months, the one hard blocker for the build. Page count (104) far above the 25 sector and product pages the quote describes. Revision rounds: 3 said in the meeting [T 06:53], 2 in the quote [E]. Directors sign off together but have not been on a call. Forms: signature, 6th form and branching not quoted.

14.politics.v: Isabella is the firm's first marketing hire and PWD's internal champion; her standing depends on this landing. Directors fear scope creep

14.legal.v: Downloadable PDFs (FSG, vulnerable clients policy) on one Financial Services page with download buttons. Privacy policy in the footer needs a formal review; Gabe said PWD would supply a standard template and advised legal review. AFSL details and compliance documents in the footer.
14.legal.contested: A standard privacy policy from PWD is not a quote line; content writing is out of scope (E).

14.gut.v: Organised, keen client doing the work on her side; the risk is her executive team, not her. Correct the revision-round wording and settle the page count with Adam before internals.

12.security.v: All PWD websites are built to the same security standard, included in the build. No premium package.
